authorship: Original Scout learning cards; referenced works inform concepts and retain their own licenses.

cards.title: Portfolio concentration
cards.summary: Position weights describe where observed capital sits. HHI is the sum of squared fractional weights; its inverse is an effective position count. A portfolio split equally between two labels has HHI 0.5.
cards.decision_use: Use get_portfolio_risk, then inspect underlying collateral and shared counterparties before deciding whether the portfolio is diversified.
cards.pitfall: Several tickers can depend on the same asset or issuer. HHI on gross labels does not capture debt, correlation or liquidity.

cards.title: Look-through exposure
cards.summary: A vault share, LP receipt or liquid staking token is a claim on underlying positions. Map the claim through each wrapper and include borrowing liabilities to understand economic exposure.
cards.decision_use: Ask for Zerion position detail, collateral, debt and ownership links. Preserve unknown exposures if the adapter only provides token labels.
cards.pitfall: Adding receipt value and its underlying assets can double-count the same capital.

cards.title: Yield components
cards.summary: A yield headline can mix borrower interest, trading fees, token rewards and price changes. Each component has a payer, payment asset and measurement window.
cards.decision_use: Use assess_defi_yield with dated user inputs. Inspect rewards ending, variable borrowing cost and entry/exit fees separately.
cards.pitfall: A quoted APY may already include compounding or rewards. Adding either again overstates the result.

cards.title: APR and APY
cards.summary: APR is a rate before a specified compounding schedule. APY includes that schedule. For periodic compounding, APY equals (1 + APR/n)^n - 1, with APR expressed as a fraction.
cards.decision_use: State the rate convention and period before comparing two products. Scout yield scenarios use simple APR with no compounding.
cards.pitfall: An annualized short sample does not promise the same rate for a year.

cards.title: Vault shares and ERC-4626
cards.summary: A tokenized vault converts deposited assets into shares. Returns depend on the assets behind each share, valuation rules, fees and withdrawal conditions.
cards.decision_use: Identify the venue, vault contract, allocator, collateral and distributor. Check assets per share and redemption limits.
cards.pitfall: A share balance is not an immediately withdrawable asset balance. Thin vaults can have donation-related pricing risks.

cards.title: Withdrawal queues
cards.summary: Some positions require a withdrawal request followed by later settlement. The time to receive spendable assets can differ from the time a share is sold or burned.
cards.decision_use: Compare the user cash deadline with queue rules, claim steps and available secondary-market depth.
cards.pitfall: Displayed NAV and instant exit proceeds can diverge, especially when many depositors leave together.

cards.title: Curator and governance risk
cards.summary: A vault curator can select collateral, limits or allocation routes. Governance and upgrade roles may have different powers and delays.
cards.decision_use: Map each power to a controller and timelock; inspect who can halt, withdraw or change collateral.
cards.pitfall: Brand recognition and an audit do not prove that control roles or current parameters are acceptable.

cards.title: Lending health factor
cards.summary: Lending protocols compare collateral value adjusted by liquidation rules with debt value. Exact formulas and collateral weights depend on the market. Aave health factor below 1 makes a position eligible for liquidation; other protocols require their own trigger rules.
cards.decision_use: Retrieve current collateral, debt, oracle prices and market parameters. Stress both collateral and debt prices, with accrued interest.
cards.pitfall: A generic portfolio drawdown cannot calculate a health factor. Missing debt or protocol parameters must stay unknown.

cards.title: Borrow utilization
cards.summary: Utilization measures how much available supply has been borrowed. Higher utilization can raise borrow rates and reduce immediately withdrawable liquidity.
cards.decision_use: Check current utilization, rate-curve parameters and exit liquidity before evaluating a leveraged carry trade.
cards.pitfall: The initial borrowing APR can change after entry, including because of the user own trade size.

cards.title: Recursive lending loops
cards.summary: A loop repeatedly borrows against supplied collateral and reinvests the proceeds. It magnifies exposure and couples yield to borrowing costs and liquidation rules.
cards.decision_use: Show gross supplied capital, debt and equity. Test incentive removal, rate increases and collateral depegs together.
cards.pitfall: The deposit APY alone hides financing cost and forced-sale risk.

cards.title: Oracle risk
cards.summary: An oracle delivers a value used by a protocol. It can represent a market price, a computed exchange rate or an administrator report, each with different failure modes.
cards.decision_use: Check update cadence, deviation rules, fallback behavior and whether liquidations use the same price the user sees.
cards.pitfall: A valid transaction containing an old or manipulable price can still cause a harmful liquidation.

cards.title: Stablecoin and depeg risk
cards.summary: A stablecoin targets a reference value through reserves, collateral or a strategy. The holder claim and redemption route determine what happens when the peg breaks.
cards.decision_use: Identify issuer, assets, liabilities and who absorbs losses. Check redemption eligibility and secondary-market depth.
cards.pitfall: Stable price history does not remove issuer, freeze, custody or collateral risk.

cards.title: Liquid staking tokens
cards.summary: A liquid staking token represents a claim linked to staked assets and their rewards. A market sale and protocol redemption can produce different proceeds and timing.
cards.decision_use: Separate staking return, exchange-rate movement, fees and discount risk. Map validator concentration and exit queues.
cards.pitfall: Holding the base asset and its staking wrapper creates overlapping exposure.

cards.title: Restaking
cards.summary: Restaking commits already-staked economic security to additional services. New operator or slashing conditions can add loss paths to the original staking position.
cards.decision_use: Map which services can impose losses, withdrawal delays and who controls allocations.
cards.pitfall: Several reward sources can share one collateral pool, so returns need not diversify the risk.

cards.title: Automated market makers
cards.summary: An AMM prices trades against pooled inventory using a rule. In a simple constant-product pool, the product of two reserve balances stays approximately constant before fees.
cards.decision_use: Inspect pool depth and the actual route quote at the proposed size.
cards.pitfall: TVL is not the same as executable depth around the current price.

cards.title: Impermanent loss
cards.summary: When relative asset prices change, an LP position rebalances and can be worth less than holding the starting assets. Fees can offset this difference, but do not guarantee it.
cards.decision_use: Compare LP total return with the same initial assets held outside the pool, including rewards, fees and withdrawal cost.
cards.pitfall: The word impermanent does not mean the loss disappears when withdrawing. Concentrated ranges change the payoff.

cards.title: Concentrated liquidity
cards.summary: A concentrated LP position supplies inventory inside selected price bounds. Outside its range it may hold mostly one asset and stop earning the expected trading fees.
cards.decision_use: Ask for range, current tick, fee accrual and rebalance costs; simulate path-dependent outcomes.
cards.pitfall: A high displayed fee APR can come from a short active window and ignore inventory loss.

cards.title: Slippage and price impact
cards.summary: Price impact is the change caused by trade size against liquidity. Slippage is the difference between a quoted expectation and final execution. A minimum-output bound limits one part of that uncertainty.
cards.decision_use: Check quote timestamp, size, route, fees and minimum received before any Zerion handoff.
cards.pitfall: Raising slippage to force a transaction through can make an unfavorable fill acceptable to the contract.

cards.title: MEV and sandwich attacks
cards.summary: Transaction ordering can create value for searchers, block builders or validators. A sandwich places trades around a victim swap to exploit its price impact and tolerance.
cards.decision_use: Use the available quote protections and assess route liquidity. Treat protection claims as provider-specific.
cards.pitfall: Private submission or a low tolerance reduces some paths without proving every form of MEV is removed.

cards.title: Bridge risk
cards.summary: Moving value across chains adds dependencies on message verification, finality, relayers and sometimes custodians. A bridged token can have a different claim from a native issuance. OP Stack canonical withdrawals require a proof and fault-challenge period before L1 finalization; faster liquidity routes have different risks.
cards.decision_use: Map origin, destination, asset identity, bridge contract and return path. Check current status and destination gas.
cards.pitfall: Splitting assets across chains can increase shared bridge exposure rather than reduce it.

cards.title: Finality and confirmations
cards.summary: A transaction being accepted, included and finalized are different observations. Finality assumptions depend on the chain and any cross-chain route.
cards.decision_use: Retain the transaction hash and verify the relevant terminal state with the provider before saying complete.
cards.pitfall: A timeout leaves an unknown outcome; resubmitting without reconciliation can duplicate an action.

cards.title: Ethereum gas
cards.summary: Gas measures EVM work. Fee cost depends on gas used and the effective price per gas, with base and priority components under EIP-1559.
cards.decision_use: Get a current estimate on the selected chain and keep native gas available.
cards.pitfall: A gas figure in a skill is a historical example. Fees differ across chains and time.

cards.title: Layer 2 risk
cards.summary: A rollup executes transactions with settlement mechanisms anchored to another chain. Sequencing, proofs, upgrades and withdrawal paths create distinct dependencies.
cards.decision_use: Identify the actual rollup, bridge and exit conditions for each holding.
cards.pitfall: Using the same token symbol on two networks does not imply equal settlement or liquidity risk.

cards.title: Token approvals and permits
cards.summary: An ERC-20 allowance lets a spender transfer tokens within granted conditions. Typed-data signatures can authorize permissions without immediately sending an onchain transaction.
cards.decision_use: Inspect spender, token, amount, chain, deadline and the meaning of each signed message.
cards.pitfall: A signature request can grant financial authority even when it is described as a login or contains no gas fee.

cards.title: ERC-20 decimals and identity
cards.summary: ERC-20 token balances are integers scaled by decimals. Asset identity depends on the contract and chain; symbols are display labels.
cards.decision_use: Resolve contract and decimals from current trusted metadata before quoting amounts or planning actions.
cards.pitfall: Assuming every token has 18 decimals can create orders many powers of ten too large.

cards.title: Account abstraction
cards.summary: Account abstraction supports programmable account validation and transaction handling. A paymaster may sponsor eligible fees under its own rules.
cards.decision_use: Identify the wallet implementation, bundler, supported chain and sponsorship limits.
cards.pitfall: A sponsored fee does not make the transaction free of asset, approval or contract risk.

cards.title: x402 data payments
cards.summary: x402 lets an HTTP resource request payment before serving data. In Scout the configured payment wallet pays for Zerion analytics within its spend limits.
cards.decision_use: Separate data budget from investment capital. Inspect accepted network, recipient, amount, expiry and payment result.
cards.pitfall: Paying for portfolio data grants no authority to trade the observed portfolio.

cards.title: Solana accounts
cards.summary: Solana stores state in accounts with lamports, data and an owner program. Program ownership determines which program can change the data under runtime rules.
cards.decision_use: Distinguish the wallet address, data accounts and the program that controls each account.
cards.pitfall: Account ownership by a program is different from possession of a wallet signing key.

cards.title: Program derived addresses
cards.summary: A PDA is derived from seeds and a program ID and has no ordinary private key. The deriving program can authorize for it through runtime rules using matching seeds.
cards.decision_use: Check the program ID, seeds, bump and ownership constraints when reviewing a PDA-controlled position.
cards.pitfall: A PDA-looking address alone proves neither ownership nor that the intended program validated its seeds.

cards.title: Cross-program invocation
cards.summary: A CPI lets one Solana program invoke another while passing selected accounts and privileges. Caller checks and downstream program behavior both affect the result.
cards.decision_use: Trace the target program and each writable or signer account in a transaction.
cards.pitfall: A trusted top-level program does not make every downstream account or invoked program trustworthy.

cards.title: Solana token accounts
cards.summary: A token account holds a balance for one mint and has an authority. An associated token account is the conventional derived account for a wallet, mint and token program.
cards.decision_use: Resolve mint, token program and recipient token account before preparing a transfer.
cards.pitfall: The recipient wallet address and its token account address are distinct concepts.

cards.title: Token-2022 extensions
cards.summary: Token-2022 extends token behavior with optional features such as transfer fees or hooks. These features can alter amounts received or requirements for transfers. A permanent delegate can transfer or burn tokens from any account for that mint; the token-account holder cannot revoke that mint-level authority for their account.
cards.decision_use: Inspect mint extensions and all authorities before assessing tradability or accepting a quote. Distinguish an ordinary revocable account delegate from a mint-level permanent delegate.
cards.pitfall: A familiar ticker does not establish compatibility with a venue or the absence of transfer restrictions.

cards.title: Compute units and priority fees
cards.summary: Solana transactions have compute budgets, and priority pricing is expressed per compute unit. Requested compute limits can affect fee cost.
cards.decision_use: Use simulation and a current fee estimate for the exact transaction shape.
cards.pitfall: A copied priority fee is not a reliable estimate under different congestion or compute settings.

cards.title: Recent blockhash expiry
cards.summary: A recent blockhash gives a transaction a limited validity window. A durable nonce provides a different validity mechanism with its own account state.
cards.decision_use: Track the signed transaction, signature status and last valid block height before deciding whether a retry is safe.
cards.pitfall: A client timeout alone does not prove that a signed transaction failed to land.

cards.title: Solana commitment levels
cards.summary: Solana RPC commitment levels describe confidence in observed ledger state. Processed, confirmed and finalized results have different rollback exposure.
cards.decision_use: Report the commitment used for balances and transaction verification.
cards.pitfall: Mixing a processed balance with finalized history can create an apparent accounting mismatch.

cards.title: Wrapped SOL
cards.summary: Wrapped SOL represents native SOL within the token-account model so programs can handle it alongside other tokens.
cards.decision_use: Account for wrapping, synchronization and closing steps in a transaction preview.
cards.pitfall: A token-account balance and native lamports can require separate handling; avoid counting the same SOL twice.

cards.title: Solana mint authorities
cards.summary: Mint and freeze authorities can affect supply and account usability. Other authority types control account operations or extension behavior.
cards.decision_use: Inspect current authorities and whether they are revoked, multisig-controlled or upgradeable.
cards.pitfall: A revoked mint authority alone does not establish that a token is safe to trade.

cards.title: Perpetual futures and funding
cards.summary: Perpetual contracts maintain exposure without a fixed expiry and use funding payments or other mechanisms to track an index. Margin and liquidation use venue rules.
cards.decision_use: Separate price PnL, funding, fees and collateral risk. Inspect the mark price and maintenance requirements. Label a supplied funding schedule as a scenario; future funding magnitude and sign can change.
cards.pitfall: Positive historical funding is not a locked return and can reverse while a position is open.

cards.title: Cash-and-carry basis
cards.summary: A basis trade pairs offsetting exposures to earn a price or funding difference. Profit depends on financing, execution and maintaining the hedge.
cards.decision_use: Identify both legs, margin locations, basis convergence assumptions and a path to unwind each side.
cards.pitfall: Small directional delta does not remove liquidation, custody, funding or cross-venue risk.

cards.title: Position sizing and risk budget
cards.summary: A trading risk budget defines an acceptable planned loss before choosing position size. For a simple spot trade, size depends on the distance to invalidation plus realistic costs.
cards.decision_use: Record thesis, invalidation, size cap, liquidity and expected holding period before a proposal.
cards.pitfall: Stops are instructions whose fills can slip. Planned loss is not a guaranteed maximum loss.

cards.title: Backtest validity
cards.summary: A backtest evaluates rules on historical observations under a fill and cost model. Separating development data from later test data reduces selection bias.
cards.decision_use: Use time-ordered holdouts, fees, slippage and realistic availability of assets and signals.
cards.pitfall: Trying many strategies and reporting only the winner overstates the evidence, even when its chart looks strong.

cards.title: Drawdown and recovery
cards.summary: Drawdown is the fall from a prior equity peak. After a 50% loss, recovering the original value requires a 100% gain on the remaining capital.
cards.decision_use: Use a dated equity series that accounts for deposits and withdrawals before comparing strategies.
cards.pitfall: PnL from acquisition cost and peak-to-trough drawdown measure different things.

cards.title: Exit liquidity and market depth
cards.summary: Liquidity describes the ability to trade a particular size at a particular cost and time. Depth can disappear during stress when it is needed most.
cards.decision_use: Compare the user planned exit size with executable quotes and withdrawal capacity.
cards.pitfall: High volume or TVL can coexist with a costly exit; printed metrics can include activity that is hard to realize.

cards.title: Trade thesis and journal
cards.summary: A journal records the reason for a trade, expected holding period, entry criteria, invalidation and later outcomes. It helps separate a repeatable rule from a lucky result.
cards.decision_use: Write the plan before entry; review decisions against information available at that time.
cards.pitfall: Rewriting the thesis after a loss makes strategy evaluation unreliable.

cards.title: Zerion action boundary
cards.summary: Zerion AI supplies its own wallet and action workflows. Scout currently produces portfolio proposals and does not call its trading CLI.
cards.decision_use: Keep Scout action plans on Zerion. A future adapter must bind a specific intent, approval, quote expiry and verified outcome.
cards.pitfall: Installing the official Zerion plugin alongside Scout gives the host additional tools; Scout cannot police every other plugin.

cards.title: Tokenized real-world claims
cards.summary: A token can represent a claim on offchain assets whose settlement, valuation and redemption depend on an issuer and legal agreements.
cards.decision_use: Read eligibility, claim priority, pricing cadence, redemption windows and custody arrangements.
cards.pitfall: A transferable token does not guarantee that every buyer has a direct right to redeem the underlying asset.

cards.title: Principal and yield tokens
cards.summary: Some systems split a yield-bearing claim into a principal claim and a claim on yield until maturity. Each side inherits the underlying asset and protocol risks.
cards.decision_use: Inspect maturity, redemption units, underlying exchange-rate behavior and exit liquidity.
cards.pitfall: A discounted principal token can carry depeg or redemption risk even when the implied rate looks fixed.

cards.title: Correlation and shared risks
cards.summary: Correlation measures how a pair of returns move together over a chosen period. Shared collateral, leverage and liquidity channels can align losses during stress.
cards.decision_use: Use comparable return series and inspect common issuers, chains and debt dependencies alongside historical correlation.
cards.pitfall: An effective position count based on weights does not measure correlation-adjusted diversification.
